paragraphs: St Albans has two councils. The city and district council handles bins, council tax and housing, while Hertfordshire County Council is responsible for social care, so the council fostering service for St Albans families is the county's Hertfordshire Fostering Service. The independent agencies shown above also approve carers in and around the city. Hertfordshire takes first enquiries through Foster East, a recruitment network of 11 councils in the East of England.

The county says it has more than 900 children in care, many of whom need a foster family. A St Albans Times feature in September 2025, which spoke to carers in the city, reported that Hertfordshire had fewer than 400 fostering households. The council looks for carers for short-term care of a few weeks up to two years, emergency care of about ten days, long-term care for children who cannot go home, weekend sleepover breaks, and teenagers who have arrived in the UK separated from their families. Its NEST scheme, modelled on the Mockingbird approach, links six fostering households to care for children who would otherwise live in a children's home.

New carers get preparation training, their own social worker with monthly supervision, an experienced carer as a buddy, local support groups and an out-of-hours line every day of the week. Most training courses run at county offices in Stevenage or Apsley. The council pays a weekly skills payment and an allowance of up to £468 a week for each child, with extras for birthdays, holidays, mileage and setting up. Emergency carers receive a £75 daily retainer whether or not a child is placed.

You need to be over 21, in good general health and to have a spare room; you can keep working for some types of fostering. Hertfordshire runs online information evenings, with the next listed for Thursday 10 December 2026. Speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies above before you decide.
